newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian senators against proposed budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Russian senators against proposed budget cuts.

text.p: The head of the Federation Council, Russia's upper house of parliament, said on Tuesday his chamber opposed budget spending cuts proposed by the government, Prime-Tass news agency reported.
It quoted Yegor Stroyev as saying the Federation Council was preparing a letter to President Boris Yeltsin asking him not to carry out proposed sequestration, or spending cuts.
Stroyev said the government should at least avoid cuts in the funding of social benefits and financing of Russian regions.

Last week the Russian government approved a plan to cut spending in its 1997 budget, necessitated by a shortfall of revenue, which was less than 60 percent of budgeted levels for the first quarter of this year.

Under the 1997 budget law, if revenues in any quarter are below 90 percent of planned levels, the government must present a bill on sequestering to the State Duma lower house, which is dominated by communists and conservatives.

Many Duma deputies have said they will vote against the proposed cuts. But the Federation Council, where many Kremlin supporters and more moderate conservatives have seats, had been considered less likely to protest against the decision.
